fields.name: Display name
fields.syncIntervalHint: How often filex walks this storage for changes made outside it (poll mode). Leave empty for the server default (15 minutes). A large, rarely changing storage is happier with a long interval; a scan that outlasts its interval is not started twice.
fields.rbacHint: When on, non-admins see only files/folders explicitly granted to them via the permissions panel. When off, the storage is open to all users (capability by role).
fields.nameChangedWarning: Clients address this storage by name. Renaming it changes the WebDAV, SFTP, S3 and NFS paths — a mount or bookmark using the old name will start answering 404 until you update it.
fields.stableAddressHint: Mounts and scripts can use this instead of the name. It is assigned once and never changes, so renaming the storage does not break them.

fieldHelp.path: Directory on the server. It is created if missing; filex never mounts /.
fieldHelp.prefix: Sub-folder inside the bucket. Required: filex never takes ownership of the bucket root.
fieldHelp.root: Sub-folder on the backend. Required: filex never mounts the account root.
fieldHelp.endpoint: Leave empty for AWS S3. Any S3-compatible store needs its endpoint.
fieldHelp.pathStyle: On for every non-AWS store. It is turned on automatically when an endpoint is set and this was never touched.
fieldHelp.disablePresign: On by default: uploads and the downloads behind public share links stream through filex, so the bucket endpoint never has to be reachable from a browser (a LAN-only MinIO just works). Turn it off only when the endpoint is reachable from your users' browsers (AWS, a public MinIO) and you want them to talk to the bucket directly — faster for very large files, and the store must accept SDK-signed URLs (Ceph RGW / some Hetzner setups answer SignatureDoesNotMatch).
fieldHelp.sftpAuth: Either a password or a private key is required.
fieldHelp.keyPath: Path to a key file on the server, read when the storage starts. Used when the PEM field is empty.
fieldHelp.knownHosts: OpenSSH known_hosts path for strict host-key checking. Default is trust-on-first-use in ~/.filex/known_hosts.
fieldHelp.hostKey: A single public key in authorized_keys / known_hosts line form.
fieldHelp.insecureSkipHostKey: Accepts any host key. Only for throwaway hosts.
fieldHelp.tls: Plain FTP sends credentials in the clear — turn this on whenever the server supports it.
fieldHelp.passive: Off switches to active mode, which needs the server to dial back into this host.
fieldHelp.smbShare: The share name alone, without the server: `media`, not `\nas\media`.
fieldHelp.smbDomain: Only for a Windows domain account. Leave empty for a NAS.
fieldHelp.smbRoot: Sub-folder inside the share. Leave empty for the whole share.

threeAddresses.title: Three machines, three addresses
threeAddresses.browser: Your browser loads the editor's JavaScript straight from the document server URL below, so that address has to work in a browser — not only inside the container network.
threeAddresses.server: The filex process fetches the document server's health endpoint from the same URL. This is what the Test button checks.
threeAddresses.callback: The document server fetches the document from filex and posts the save back to filex's public URL, so that address has to work from inside the document server's container:
threeAddresses.diagnose: When something fails, these two commands say which half is wrong:
threeAddresses.fromWorkstation: from a workstation — the browser leg
threeAddresses.fromDocumentServer: from inside the document server container — the callback leg

legs.callback: From the document server back to filex:
legs.cannotCheck: not checked — filex cannot make the document server issue a request on demand. The warnings below are the shapes that certainly cannot work.
legs.disagree: filex reaches this address and your browser does not. That is what a container-internal name looks like: the editor loads in the browser, so it will fail there.
legs.callbackOk: reached filex — the document server downloaded a test file from it
legs.callbackBad: did NOT reach filex. The document opens and the save never comes back.
legs.callbackUnchecked: could not be measured; the warnings below are the shapes that certainly cannot work.

browserStates.wrongContent: something answered, but it is not this service
browserStates.timeout: timed out — nothing answered and nothing refused
browserStates.mixedContent: blocked: this admin page is HTTPS and that address is HTTP

advisories.browser_bare_host: “{host}” is a single-label host name. filex can reach it from inside the container network, but your browser loads this service directly and cannot resolve it. Use an address a browser can open.
advisories.browser_loopback_host: This is a loopback address, but filex is published at {publicUrl} — the people who open it are not on this host, and to their browser “{host}” means their own machine.
advisories.public_url_loopback: The document server fetches the document from filex and posts the save back to {publicUrl}. Inside its own container that address is the document server, not filex.
advisories.public_url_bare_host: filex's public URL ({publicUrl}) is a container-network name. The document server can reach it, but share links and e-mails built from it will not open in a browser outside that network.
advisories.public_url_unresolved: filex itself cannot resolve “{host}”. That is expected if your document server uses a different DNS view; otherwise the public URL points at a name nothing can look up.

demo.title: filex — self-hosted file manager that embeds anywhere
demo.subtitle: One Go binary with a full web UI, pluggable storage/auth/DB drivers, real-time collaboration, an embeddable web component, a desktop app with background folder sync, and a built-in MCP server so AI agents can drive it natively.
demo.sandbox: Shared sandbox — everything resets nightly, and adding storages or plugins is disabled here.
demo.adminHint: Sign in with a non-demo account for full admin.
demo.alsoIncluded: Also included: RBAC with per-file and per-folder grants · multi-tenancy · OIDC SSO and LDAP / Active Directory · in-place viewers and editors, Office through OnlyOffice · creating a document from + New — Markdown, text, CSV and code anywhere, Word, Excel, PowerPoint and OpenDocument wherever OnlyOffice is connected · a whole selection downloaded as one streamed archive · trash and versioning · replication · quotas · audit log · webhooks and in-app notifications · storage plugins · a persistent operation queue · a usage and cost view built from your storage provider's own daily report.

features.storageBody: Mount local disks, S3, SFTP, WebDAV, FTP/FTPS and SMB/NAS side by side as one tree — then reach that same tree back as S3, SFTP, FTPS, NFSv3 or WebDAV.
features.searchBody: Permission-aware full-text search across every storage. Try “budget 2026” for Documents/Budget-2026.csv, or “mian.go” — one typo forgiven — for Code/main.go. Tag a file and tag:yourlabel filters by it.
features.shareBody: Public links with a PIN, an expiry and a download limit, inbound drop links that collect files from other people — plus end-to-end encrypted folders the server cannot read.
features.desktopBody: The same explorer as a Windows, Linux or macOS app: several accounts at once, two-way background sync from the tray, a portable build on every platform for machines you may not install software on, and “filex mount” to attach a remote server as a Linux folder or a Windows drive.
features.embedBody: Drop the real file manager into your product as a Vue 3, React or framework-free web component, and hand AI agents a token-scoped REST surface and a native MCP server.

share.title: Share links

av.title: Antivirus
av.desc: Files written to filex are scanned in the background with ClamAV — reached either through a scanner binary on this server or through a clamd daemon over the network or a unix socket. Infected files are moved to the trash and a file.infected event is emitted. Scanning never blocks a write.
av.setupHint: No scanner is configured. Pick a mode below, or see:

maxScan.title: Largest file scanned
maxScan.desc: Files bigger than this are skipped, not blocked — they are stored and served as usual, they are simply never handed to ClamAV. In binary mode each file is copied to a temporary file before the scanner runs, so this is a disk and time budget there as well as a policy; in daemon mode the bytes are streamed straight to clamd.
maxScan.label: Megabytes
maxScan.hint: Between {min} and {max} MB. Takes effect on the next file scanned, with no restart.
maxScan.errRange: Enter a whole number between {min} and {max}.

window.title: Editor save-scan window
window.desc: A file created in the built-in text editor is scanned straight away. A save to a file that already exists schedules one scan this many minutes later, and further saves inside that window join it rather than queueing more — so a burst of Ctrl+S costs one scan, and that scan reads the file's final state. The trade: a saved file can sit unscanned for up to this long after the last save.
window.label: Minutes
window.hint: Between {min} and {max} minutes. Takes effect immediately, with no restart; scans already scheduled keep their original time.
window.errRange: Enter a whole number between {min} and {max}.

av.restartPending: Saved. The antivirus switch, mode and address take effect the next time the server restarts — until then it keeps running with the configuration it started with.

power.label: Scan uploaded files
power.desc: Takes effect at the next restart, in both directions — turning this on does not start scanning, and turning it off does not stop it, until the server is restarted.
power.onAtRestart: Antivirus scanning will be enabled the next time the server restarts.
power.offAtRestart: Antivirus scanning will be disabled the next time the server restarts.

transport.label: How ClamAV is reached

hint.binary: Runs a scanner found on this server's PATH. Set FILEX_CLAMAV_BIN to name a specific one.
hint.daemon: Streams each file to a running clamd. Use this when ClamAV is its own container — no shared filesystem is needed.

transport.addrHint: host:port (port 3310 if omitted), or a unix socket path such as /var/run/clamav/clamd.ctl.
transport.binaryNote: The scanner binary itself stays an environment setting (FILEX_CLAMAV_BIN): it is a path this server executes, so it is deliberately not editable here.
transport.errAddrRequired: Daemon mode needs a clamd address.
transport.savedAtRestart: Saved. The new transport takes effect the next time the server restarts.

The storage itself is not deleted. | Remove the plugin “{name}”? {count} storages use its driver and will stop opening until it is installed again. The storages themselves are not deleted.
plugins.errFile: Choose the plugin binary to upload

plugins.trustWarning: A plugin runs with filex's own privileges and is handed the credentials of every storage created on it. Install only plugins you trust.
plugins.supertenantOnly: Storage plugins are managed by the platform operator.
plugins.disabled: Storage plugins are disabled on this instance.

conformance.unverifiedHint: No report: the plugin offers no self-test endpoint, or verification is off on this instance. Nothing failed — nothing was checked.
conformance.refusedNote: A plugin that fails its own claims is refused: filex will not offer half a driver as a whole one. Fix the probe below and install the new build.

mode.warn: Verification is in “warn” mode on this instance: a plugin that fails its own claims is installed anyway and only written to the log. The safety net is down.
mode.off: Verification is off on this instance: nothing checks that a plugin does what it claims before a storage is built on it. The safety net is down.

load.waitedTitle: Calls that had to queue for a free slot. A plugin that is merely slow shows up here before it shows up as an error.
load.rejectedTitle: Callers that gave up waiting for a free slot and were answered with an error. Find out why the plugin is slow, or raise its concurrency limit.
load.rejectingBanner: Refusing operations: {names}. Every slot is busy, so callers are being turned away with an error rather than queued.

upgrade.rollback: The upgrade failed. The previous binary was put back, so nothing was lost.

prefs.languageHint: Applies here right away, and is saved on your account for the next browser you sign in from.
prefs.compactHint: Tighter rows in the file explorer.
prefs.timezoneHint: Dates are stored as a moment in time and shown on the clock you pick here, so everyone sees the same instant on their own clock. Saved to your account, so it follows you to another browser.
prefs.startPageHint: Where filex opens when you sign in or go to the front door. Following a link straight to a page still takes you there.
prefs.modeHint: Which variant is painted. Auto follows your operating system.
prefs.paletteHint: Which colours that variant is made of. Every palette has a light and a dark version, so this and the setting above work together.
prefs.folderMemoryHint: A folder opens the way you last left it — list or grid, and its sort. Off by default; your last choice applies everywhere instead.
prefs.openTriggerHint: How a mouse opens a file. On a touchscreen a tap always opens, and the checkbox always selects.
prefs.desktopAppHint: The reminder in the corner of the app can be closed for good — these downloads stay here.

notifications.eventsHint: Turning one off keeps it out of your bell. Nothing stops being recorded — an administrator still sees every event.

events.file_infected: A virus is found in a file
events.file_deleted: A file is deleted for good
events.file_trashed: A file goes to the trash
events.file_moved: A file is moved or renamed
events.drop_received: A file arrives through a request link
events.e2e_escrow_used: An encrypted folder is opened with the escrow key

userSettings.heading: User settings
userSettings.headingSub: Manage your profile, preferences, and security.

ai.body: This release has no per-user assistant settings. The AI features filex does ship are configured for the whole instance by an administrator, so there is nothing here for you to turn on or off yet.
